description: Repeated load/execute/unload cycles under concurrent traditional + containerized-seam (hybrid) execution; per-cycle leak detection via WeakReference survival, resident plugin assemblies (with their AssemblyLoadContext), managed memory and GC collection counts. Two phases: shipped configuration (documents expected leak) and collectible-path (stub validator, isolates the collectible ALC machinery).

collectiblePath.validator: NonLoadingSecurityValidator (harness stub; performs NO security checks - measurement-only)

summary.verdict: no leak indicators: every cycle's plugin instances, types and assemblies were collected after unload
leak indicators in all 30 cycles - plugin assemblies remain resident in the DEFAULT (non-collectible) AssemblyLoadContext; see architecturalFinding

shippedConfigurationVerdict.verdict: leak indicators in all 30 cycles - plugin assemblies remain resident in the DEFAULT (non-collectible) AssemblyLoadContext; see architecturalFinding

collectiblePathVerdict.verdict: no leak indicators: every cycle's plugin instances, types and assemblies were collected after unload

summary.architecturalFinding: In the shipped configuration every plugin assembly passes through DefaultPluginSecurityValidator.ValidateAssemblyAsync, which uses Assembly.LoadFrom(path) and therefore pins the assembly in the DEFAULT (non-collectible) AssemblyLoadContext; FilePluginLoader then reuses that pinned copy instead of its collectible PluginLoadContext copy. UnloadAllPlugins is consequently a no-op for the plugin assemblies actually in use, and the collectible ALC path is never exercised unless validation avoids loading the file. This is a measurable, reproducible property of the shipped code (see shippedConfiguration cycles), not a harness artifact.
summary.verdictScope: plugin implementation assemblies (the collectible ALC path); the shared plugin interface assembly (PluginImplementations.dll) intentionally resides in the default context in all phases
summary.hybridExecutionNote: Containerized-seam executions use an in-memory orchestrator (CRPCF dispatch path only, no container); a real container backend adds its own lifecycle that this measurement does not cover
